cards.text: Jesus just fed four thousand men, besides women and children, with seven loaves and a few small fish. Then He sails to Magadan, and the Pharisees and Sadducees show up. They're two groups of Jewish religious leaders, and they're here to test Him.

cards.question: The Pharisees and Sadducees come to test Jesus. What do they ask Him to show them?

cards.text: A SIGN? He just turned seven loaves into dinner for four thousand, and I can't make seven cookies feed MYSELF. Jesus answers with the weather: when evening comes, they say it'll be fair, because the sky is red.

cards.question: In the morning, they say a red and overcast sky means a stormy day is coming.
Jesus tells the Pharisees and Sadducees they know how to read the sky. What does He say they can't read?

cards.text: Then Jesus says a wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign. But they're only getting one.

cards.question: Jesus says this generation will be given only one sign. Who is that sign named after?

cards.text: That's Jonah, the prophet who spent three days and three nights in a great fish, and I used to complain about a DRAWER. Back in Matthew 12, Jesus said that just like Jonah in the fish, the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

cards.question: After telling the Pharisees and Sadducees about the sign of Jonah, Jesus stays to keep debating them.

cards.text: Nope. Jesus left them and went away. No encore. Then He and the disciples cross to the other side, and the disciples forgot to pack something. Something IMPORTANT.

cards.question: Jesus and the disciples cross to the other side. What did the disciples forget to take?

cards.text: They forgot the BREAD. Then Jesus says, “Watch out!” and “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.” Leaven? Now He's talking baker talk, and my mustache just stood straight up.

cards.question: The disciples talk it over and decide Jesus said it because they didn't bring any ___.
Jesus is aware of what the disciples are discussing among themselves.

cards.text: Jesus calls them “You of little faith” and asks why they're debating about having no bread. Friend, that's like standing right next to my oven, panicking about where I'm gonna bake.

cards.question: Jesus asks if they still don't understand, and if they don't remember the ___ loaves for the five thousand.

cards.text: Then He reminds them of the seven loaves for the four thousand, the meal they JUST saw. He asks how many basketfuls they gathered both times, and you could hear a crumb drop in that boat.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples He was talking about bread all along.

cards.text: Not bread. Jesus says it again: “But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.” And FINALLY, the light comes on in that boat.

cards.question: The disciples understand that the leaven Jesus warned them about is the ___ of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus fed the crowd with 'seven loaves and a few small fish.' 'A few small fish' comes from Matthew 15:34, but the card's citation starts at 15:36, which only says 'the fish.'

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card is three sentences: 'A SIGN?', the seven-loaves joke, and 'Jesus answers with the weather...'. Every story card after the opening card is limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card states a Bible fact, that Jesus turned seven loaves into dinner for four thousand (Matthew 15:36-38). The card cites only Matthew 16:2.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card states that Jonah 'spent three days and three nights in a great fish.' That fact comes from Jonah 1:17, but the card cites only Matthew 12:40.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card packs in several sentences and fragments: 'Nope.', 'Jesus left them and went away.', 'No encore.', the crossing sentence, and 'Something IMPORTANT.' That is more than 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card is four sentences: 'They forgot the BREAD.', 'Then Jesus says...', 'Leaven?', and the mustache line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card places the conversation 'in that boat.' Matthew 16:5 says 'When they crossed to the other side,' which points to them having already arrived. The text never puts this exchange in the boat.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card again places the disciples 'in that boat,' though Matthew 16:5 says they had crossed to the other side. The card is also three sentences: 'Not bread.', 'Jesus says it again...', and 'And FINALLY...'.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
